bull.b: Rapid TTR revenue growth shows strong commercial traction for Alnylam’s marketed franchise and expanding demand in ATTR cardiomyopathy. Continued uptake provides a durable revenue base, while scale can support investment in additional RNAi medicines and broader patient access.

Clinical outcome evidence and a convenient quarterly dosing profile strengthen AMVUTTRA’s differentiation in a serious rare disease. These characteristics can support physician adoption, patient persistence, and the company’s ability to build a lasting position in TTR treatment.

Strong operating and free cash flow gives Alnylam internal funding capacity for clinical development, commercialization, and pipeline expansion. Free cash flow representing about 86% of net income also supports the durability of the current profitability inflection and strategic flexibility.

bear.b: Slower conversion of physician interest into patient starts may delay the realization of AMVUTTRA’s commercial opportunity. If newer prescribers remain less familiar with ATTR-CM or have limited eligible patients, growth investment may produce a more gradual and costly ramp.

Higher royalty costs are reducing product gross margin, while collaboration revenue can be volatile after a prior one-time Roche milestone. This mix creates pressure on earnings quality and makes reported operating performance more dependent on product scale and recurring sales.

A change in commercial leadership adds execution risk while Alnylam is still working to improve AMVUTTRA conversion and prepare future launches. Transition time could disrupt accountability or go-to-market momentum, even though the existing organization provides a foundation for continuity.
